title: AI News Weekly Recap — August 16, 2026
summary: The week's clearest through-line was OpenAI testing how much danger it can hold at once: it flagged its unreleased Astra model as the first it's ever treated as approaching the 'Critical' cyber tier of its own risk framework, shipped a deliberately less-restricted cyber model anyway, gated that model behind hardware security keys by Friday, and lost two more C-suite executives — its sixth and seventh exits in months — just as its public IPO filing neared a roughly $1 trillion valuation target. Around that story, the race to put frontier-grade AI on a single GPU accelerated across Meta, NVIDIA, Alibaba, and Google; the US-China price war flipped, with OpenAI and Anthropic cutting prices even as DeepSeek hiked its own by up to 1,100%; Anthropic posted its first-ever operating profit while chasing its largest acquisition yet; and AI agents kept acquiring real-world bodies — shopping, calling stores, and in one case hacking a gym's booking system to jump a waitlist.
